title: The checklist: what the published rules settle
question: For each point the permit records could not settle, what do the City's published rules say?
finding: Of 11 open points, the published rules confirm 7, contradict 0 and are silent on 4. Confirmed: Planning approval comes before the building permit application; a permit lasts 365 days and an application 730; work without a permit costs nine times the issuance fee; premium plan review is sold at half the plan review fee plus $1,000; public discretionary review is listed at $807 for FY2026–27, subject to the neighborhood organization waiver. Not found: any true catch-22, who may buy premium review, how reviewers are assigned, and what permit consultants must report.
how: Each item in the toConfirm list of the site’s “How the permit process works” page was searched for in the saved rule pages, fee tables and ordinance texts. The answer is in plain words; the quotation is copied from the saved text and checked by the script; amounts are read from the fee tables when the script runs.
limits: "Confirmed" means a published page, table or ordinance says so; where an item has several parts, the answer says which parts were found and which were not. "Not found" means silence in what the City publishes on these sites, not that no rule exists: the consolidated codes and Ethics Commission rules were not available. Scanned ordinances were read through an imperfect text layer.

rows.question: Which approvals the codes require before a building permit can be filed or issued (Planning approval, neighborhood notice, environmental review), and which street and sidewalk permits require an issued building permit first: the data shows the cross-references, not the legal order.
rows.says: Confirmed for Planning: where a project needs Planning approval, the pages say it must be obtained before the building permit application is submitted, and Planning runs the neighbor notice as part of its review. For street and sidewalk permits the order is mostly left unstated: the Street Space permit page and the Public Works completeness checklist of August 2026 do not ask for an issued building permit; only sub-sidewalk basement work is told to get the building permit first.
rows.quote: When Planning Department approval is required, you must obtain that approval prior to submitting a building permit.

source.t: Building Inspection: Request a new building address

rows.question: Whether any two permits each require the other first (a true catch-22): for example, a street-space or encroachment permit that needs an issued building permit while the building permit's issue is held for Public Works sign-off. The routing shows Public Works reviewing before issue and its own permits quoting the building application; the rules must say which comes first.
rows.says: No pair of published pages says each permit needs the other first. Where pages point at each other they give the order: the building permit is applied for first, street permits follow, and all must be issued before the certificate of occupancy. The Public Works fee schedule ties its sidewalk conformity inspection to a building permit application, not the other way round.
rows.quote: apply for a DBI building permit first, before applying for the Street Improvement and Minor Sidewalk Encroachment Permits
rows.verdict: not found in the published rules

rows.question: The life of a building permit and of an application (when each expires), the fee to extend, renew or reinstate one, and whether a 'final inspection only' permit is charged on the full job value: needed to cost the permits-to-finish-permits loop.
rows.says: An application expires if no permit is issued within 730 days of filing. An issued permit stays active for 365 days and each passed inspection extends it by another 365. A 180-day extension costs $415 each plus 20% of Plan Review Fees for an application and $228 each plus 10% of Building Permit Inspection Fees for a permit (2026 table). An expired permit cannot be extended and must be renewed. What a renewal or a 'final inspection only' permit costs, and whether it is charged on the full job value, is not in the 2026 tables; the 2024 fee ordinance listed restarting work that never began at 75% of current fee for the permit plus the full plan review fee. These time limits apply to applications filed on or after June 21, 2026 (Ordinance 259-25).
rows.quote: Once your permit is issued, it remains active for 365 days … If a permit is not issued within 730 days, your application will expire.

source.t: Building Inspection: Permit Application Timelines, Expiration and Extensions

rows.question: The fee schedule for each named fee (Building Inspection Table 1A, Planning, Fire, Public Works, Public Health) by year, to turn revenue lines into what one applicant pays for one job, and to date each fee increase.
rows.says: Only today's tables are published in full: Building Inspection (2026), Planning, Public Works, Fire and Public Health. Earlier years are mostly not posted. Planning prints its application fees for two years and its development impact fees for 2018 to 2026; the 2024 Building Inspection fee ordinance is on file as a scan. Most past increases therefore cannot be dated from the published tables alone.
rows.quote: The following building permit fees apply to all building permits issued on and after July 12, 2026.

source.t: Building Inspection: Table 1A-A, building permit fees (2026)

rows.verdict: not found in the published rules

rows.question: What 'premium plan review' and other paid faster-service options cost and who may use them.
rows.says: The 2026 Building Inspection table prices premium plan review of a submitted application at 50% of Plan Review Fee plus $1,000, on top of the normal fee. Who may buy it, and how the faster service is rationed, is not stated anywhere in the tables or pages. The 2024 fee ordinance also listed an over-the-counter premium review by appointment at 50% of Plan Review Fee plus $400.00; the 2026 table no longer prints it.

source.t: Building Inspection: Table 1A-B, other building permit and plan review fees (2026)

rows.question: The penalty for work without a permit and for exceeding a permit's scope (the Controller cited two times and nine times the permit fee), and whether penalties are charged when the only fault is an expired permit.
rows.says: Confirmed: the 2026 table charges two times the permit issuance fee for exceeding a permit's scope and, for work without a permit, an investigation fee of nine times the permit issuance fee plus the original permit fee. Nothing in the tables or pages says whether the investigation fee is charged when the only fault is that a permit expired.
rows.quote: Exceeding the scope of approved permit Two times the Permit Issuance Fee … Nine times the Permit Issuance Fee plus the

source.t: Building Inspection: Table 1A-K, penalties, hearings and code enforcement assessments (2026)

rows.question: Renewal periods and fees for sidewalk tables and chairs, display, parklet, food-truck and Fire operating permits, and whether each needs proof of another permit or licence (health permit, business registration, insurance) before it is issued.
rows.says: Printed yearly charges: a parklet license per parking space ($119, $1,780 or $2,373 by type); a food truck renewal at Public Works ($199, health and fire fees extra); a street vending renewal ($115). A Fire Department annual permit runs at least 365 days and most need a current City tax license. Before Public Works finally approves a food truck it asks for business registration, $2,000,000 of liability insurance, a health certificate and a Fire Department certificate. Fees and renewal periods for sidewalk tables and chairs and merchandise displays are not in the 2026-27 Public Works schedule.
rows.quote: most annual permits require the permit holder to also possess a current tax license certificate

source.t: San Francisco Fire Department: Submittal guidelines for fire permit applications

rows.question: The rules on who may ask for discretionary review, the filing fee, and any rule against paying to withdraw a request.
rows.says: Any member of the public or a neighborhood organization may file during the notice period. The filing fee is $788 in the schedule effective August 29, 2025 and $807 in the published schedule effective August 31, 2026; a neighborhood organization on Planning's list for 24 months can have it waived. The page says the power is for exceptional and extraordinary circumstances. No rule about paying a requester to withdraw was found.
rows.quote: If a member of the public or a neighborhood organization would like the Commission to assert their discretionary powers, a DR should be filed

rows.question: Whether permit consultants must report all their work or only large projects: several filers write that they have no projects over $1 million to report, which would leave most small-job consulting undisclosed.
rows.says: Not found. The reporting rules for permit consultants are kept by the Ethics Commission and are not among the permit pages, fee tables and ordinances collected here. The Building Inspection agent disclosure form says only that the department does not regulate consultants or give them preferential treatment.
rows.quote: Department does not regulate permit expediters/consultants or afford them preferential treatment.
rows.verdict: not found in the published rules

rows.question: How plan reviews are assigned to reviewers today (rotation, district, specialty) and what changed after the 2021 Controller review, to judge the repeat reviewer-consultant pairs.
rows.says: How individual reviewers are assigned (by rotation, district or specialty) is not described in any published page. What is published is Ordinance 93-23, enacted 2023-05-26: applications are to be processed in the order received unless a written public-policy reason is recorded, applicants are to be treated the same whether or not they hire a permit consultant, and intentional preferential treatment is official misconduct.
rows.quote: other permit-related material in the order in which that type of material is received

source.t: Board of Supervisors: Ordinance 93-23, Campaign and Governmental Conduct Code - Permit Prioritization

rows.verdict: not found in the published rules

rows.question: The State deadlines for housing permits (completeness in 15 business days; comments in 30 or 60) against the City's recorded review times, which the Budget Analyst said could not be checked from the City's records.
rows.says: Confirmed, with one difference in wording: the City's page gives 15 days (it does not say business days) to tell an applicant whether a housing permit application filed after entitlement is complete, then 30 business days to approve or deny a project of 25 homes or fewer and 60 business days for 26 or more.
rows.quote: for projects 25 units and under, the local agency has 30 business days

source.t: Building Inspection: State laws streamlining building permits for new housing
